title: Arcadia Health — Case Study Outline (Draft) | Redwood Private (VPC) regulated deployment
content:
Working draft for Arcadia Health public case study + internal reference profile.

Status / open questions
- This is an outline + rough narrative only. Metrics and any architecture diagram details must be validated and approved by Arcadia before publishing.
- Open: confirm whether Arcadia will allow their logo (yes/no), and if “Arcadia Health” can be named publicly or needs anonymization (“Top 10 health system”, etc.). Current direction from kickoff: name is OK, but keep infra details high-level.
- Open: which Redwood regions + HA setup can be described (avoid specific AZ counts, subnets, internal network topology).
- Open: final spokesperson(s) and titles for the quote block.

Primary case study angle (proposed)
- “Regulated healthcare workloads in a customer VPC: predictable inference performance with enterprise controls (audit logs, key management, retention) without building the serving stack.”

Secondary angles (choose 1–2)
- Faster time-to-production for a regulated environment (Private control plane + customer-managed networking)
- Reliability + graceful degradation (fallback policies) for patient-facing / clinician-facing workflows
- Operational visibility: token-level cost/latency + incident triage (Console dashboards)

Target audience
- Enterprise platform/security leaders + ML/platform engineers evaluating LLM inference for regulated workloads.

Customer snapshot (needs customer verification)
- Company: Arcadia Health
- Industry: Healthcare
- Deployment mode: Redwood Private (VPC deployment)
- Workload type: Internal-facing clinical operations assistant + summarization (PHI-adjacent constraints; do NOT claim PHI is sent unless explicitly approved)
- Key constraints:
  - Customer-managed networking (VPC), private connectivity
  - Audit logs export requirements + retention controls
  - Key ownership / KMS integration expectations
  - Security review rigor (SOC 2 evidence, change management, access controls)

Proposed story structure (web + PDF)

1) Headline + subhead (draft copy)
- Headline options:
  A) “Arcadia Health deploys LLM inference in a private VPC with auditability and predictable performance.”
  B) “From security review to production: Arcadia Health runs regulated LLM workloads on Redwood Private.”
- Subhead options:
  A) “Using Redwood Private, Arcadia Health met VPC and audit logging requirements while maintaining consistent latency for clinician-facing workflows.”
  B) “Redwood’s private deployment model and operational tooling helped Arcadia Health standardize LLM serving without building and operating a custom inference stack.”

2) Customer challenge (bullets + narrative)
- What changed:
  - Increased demand for LLM features from internal product teams
  - Security/compliance requirements became gating for rollout
- Constraints called out in discovery/security review (paraphrase; keep neutral):
  - “We need to keep traffic private and maintain strong audit trails.”
  - “Key ownership and access controls have to align with our existing policies.”
  - “We can’t ship something that we can’t explain to auditors.”
- Pain points with prior approach (do not name vendors unless approved):
  - Too much operational overhead to self-host and keep patched
  - Difficulty proving compliance posture for a bespoke setup
  - Unpredictable latency under load; unclear fallbacks

3) Why Redwood (decision criteria)
- Non-negotiables (per Arcadia):
  - Private deployment option in customer-managed environment (VPC)
  - Audit logging and exportability
  - Key management integration approach (KMS/HSM alignment)
  - Strong security posture (SOC 2, least privilege access model) + documented processes
- Differentiators we can safely state (avoid absolute claims):
  - Unified inference API + ops tooling across deployment modes
  - Built-in observability (latency, error analysis) and rollout controls
  - Reference architecture + customer success process for regulated deployments

4) Implementation overview (what they actually did)
- Timeline (draft; verify dates):
  - Week 0–1: Security review kickoff + evidence collection
  - Week 2–3: VPC/private connectivity setup + initial workload test
  - Week 4–5: Observability + audit export validation + reliability testing
  - Week 6+: Production rollout behind feature flags
- Teams involved (Arcadia): Platform, Security/Compliance, App team for assistant workflow
- Teams involved (Redwood): AE (Avery), SE (Markus/Simran), CS (Rachel/Miguel), Security review (Naomi), Legal/comms via Camila/Soojin

5) Architecture (public-safe)
- Diagram intent: show boundaries, not internals.
- Components (label in diagram):
  - Arcadia VPC
  - Arcadia application services (assistant/summarization)
  - Private connectivity to Redwood Private control plane (within Arcadia VPC) OR “private endpoint” language depending on final deployment
  - Redwood inference runtime in private environment
  - Redwood Console/telemetry (describe as “operational dashboards and alerting”; avoid naming internal collectors)
  - Audit log export to Arcadia SIEM / storage (high level)
  - KMS integration point (customer-managed keys) (ensure wording matches what was implemented)

Architecture sketch notes (for designer)
- Keep it as 3 zones max:
  1) “Arcadia apps”
  2) “Arcadia VPC / Redwood Private deployment”
  3) “Arcadia security + compliance systems (SIEM/log archive)”
- Avoid:
  - Listing cloud provider account IDs, region/AZ names
  - Exact GPU types / counts unless Arcadia approves (likely “dedicated capacity in private environment” is enough)
  - Any mention of patient data categories (PHI) unless explicitly approved and carefully reviewed

6) Outcomes (quantified results — placeholders until validation)
Important: We should only publish metrics that have (a) a measurement window, (b) a baseline definition, (c) an owner who validated. Otherwise keep as qualitative.

Metrics table (draft placeholders)
- Latency (p50 / p95) for top 2 routes:
  - Baseline: ______ (what system, what traffic shape)
  - After Redwood: ______
  - Measurement window: ______
  - Notes: include token counts / context lengths range
  - Validation owner: Logan Wright / Simran Kaur (TBD)
- Reliability:
  - Error rate (5xx) and timeouts: baseline ______ vs after ______
  - Incident notes: any major incident during rollout? (if yes, how it was mitigated; keep honest)
  - Measurement window: ______
- Compliance/ops outcomes (likely strongest for Arcadia):
  - Audit log export configured and validated for required fields (list fields at high level only)
  - Security review time: “reduced time spent on custom evidence gathering” (if Arcadia will approve; otherwise “streamlined procurement/security review”)
- Cost:
  - Only include if Arcadia is comfortable sharing; otherwise focus on predictability + operational efficiency

Suggested “outcomes” phrasing options (safe defaults)
- “Met Arcadia’s requirements for private networking and auditability while maintaining consistent performance under production traffic.”
- “Standardized LLM inference behind a single API and operational dashboarding, reducing time spent troubleshooting and onboarding new routes.”

7) Customer quotes (candidates — must be approved word-for-word)
Candidate quote #1 (security/compliance oriented)
- “For our environment, private networking and audit trails aren’t optional. Redwood’s private deployment model let us move forward without compromising on our security requirements.”

Candidate quote #2 (engineering/ops oriented)
- “We wanted our engineers focused on building the workflow, not maintaining a custom inference stack. Redwood gave us a production-ready path in a VPC with the observability we needed.”

Candidate quote #3 (reliability oriented)
- “Having clear rollout controls and a plan for fallbacks made it easier to introduce LLM functionality into a regulated environment.”

Notes on quote sourcing
- Source call: reference program kickoff (2025-05-20). Pull exact language from transcript once Arcadia confirms spokesperson.
- Spokesperson options (unconfirmed):
  - Platform Engineering lead
  - Security/Compliance partner (less likely for public quote)

8) Proof points to collect (checklist)
- Security/compliance
  - Arcadia-approved description of key management model (KMS integration) (1–2 sentences)
  - Audit log export: list of required fields Arcadia cares about (high-level) + confirmation it’s met
  - Any language constraints (e.g., “HIPAA” mentions) — avoid unless Arcadia explicitly requests/approves
- Technical
  - Public-safe architecture diagram approval
  - Which inference features are in use (safe list): streaming, version pinning, rollout policy, fallback policy, rate limiting (only those actually used)
- Metrics
  - Baseline definition doc (what was compared, what dataset/traffic replay)
  - Screenshot candidates (Console dashboards) — likely need redaction; confirm what can be shown

9) Review + approvals plan (Arcadia + internal)
- Internal review required:
  - Soojin Lee (messaging + claims)
  - Naomi Feldman (security language)
  - Markus Klein / Simran Kaur (technical accuracy)
  - Michael Grant / Sofia Mendes (release form + final legal)
- Customer review required:
  - Spokesperson approval for quotes
  - Security/compliance approval for architecture + any compliance claims
  - Brand team approval if logo usage is included

10) Distribution plan (draft)
- Placement:
  - New Case Studies section (docs + marketing site; coordinate with Ben Carter)
  - Sales enablement: internal PDF + reference profile in HubSpot
  - Optional: cloud marketplace co-marketing (only if Arcadia opts in)
- Sales usage:
  - Use for Private/VPC deals in healthcare + other regulated verticals
  - Reference call: “private deployment + audit logging” conversations

Internal-only notes (do not publish)
- Arcadia sensitivities observed in security review:
  - Strong preference to avoid any language implying Redwood has access to customer data
  - Avoid naming specific logging backends/retention durations
  - Avoid disclosing exact deployment topology
- Support ticket context:
  - SUP-2381: audit log export format questions came up during onboarding; resolved with support + SE; this can be framed internally as “we validated audit log export meets their compliance needs.”

Next actions / owners
- Ethan (writer): convert this outline into a 1st draft narrative (web format) + list of required callouts for design
- Camila: confirm final approval path + whether Arcadia brand team needs separate review
- Avery: confirm spokesperson + title + willingness for public logo
- Markus/Simran: validate technical description + propose safe diagram labels
- Logan/Sana: propose metric measurement windows + validation approach; identify what’s publishable
- Rachel/Miguel: confirm reference-call boundaries + how often Arcadia is willing to take calls

Appendix A — Draft “About Redwood Private” blurb (for case study sidebar)
- “Redwood Private brings Redwood’s inference runtime and operational tooling into a private customer environment (VPC or on-prem), supporting customer-managed networking, audit logging, and key management integrations.”

Appendix B — Terms to avoid (until approved)
- “HIPAA compliant” (avoid unless Redwood has explicit compliance package language + Arcadia requests it)
- “PHI” (avoid unless explicitly confirmed and reviewed)
- Specific cloud provider region/AZ, GPU model/count, subnet design, or any internal service names

Appendix C — Draft section headers (web)
- Challenge
- Requirements (regulated environment)
- Solution (Redwood Private)
- Architecture (high-level)
- Results
- What’s next
